utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, The Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: May we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Stavroula Papadopoulos, and Case Manager, Thomas Laugel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hadzic, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. This Pre-Defence Conference is held pursuant to Rule 73 ter in order to make final arrangements for the commencement of the Defence case. First issue is the length of the Defence case. The Trial Chamber, in its discretion, has decided not to call upon the Defence to shorten the estimated length of the examination-in-chief of any of its witnesses, pursuant to Rule 73 ter (B); nor will the Trial Chamber determine the number of witnesses that the Defence may call, pursuant to Rule 73 ter (C). The Trial Chamber does intend to set a global time-limit for the presentation of the Defence case in-chief. It therefore invites the Defence, pursuant to Rule 73 ter (E) to make submissions regarding the time needed to present its case in-chief. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We estimated the time necessary for -- for our witnesses to 140 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 140 hours. Thank you. Does the Prosecution also wishes to make submissions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber will issue its decision on this matter very shortly. I turn to the Defence opening statement. Could the Defence indicate how much time it will need to make its opening statement, pursuant to Rule 84?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We estimate our opening statement to -- between one and a half hour and two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And we understand that Mr. Hadzic is the Defence's first witness. In light of that, could the Defence indicate whether Mr. Hadzic will be making a statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, he will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: He will.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And we estimate his statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis to -- between 30 and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have a look at the issues with regard to pending motions, and we have a preliminary remark. The Trial Chamber recalls that, at the request of the Defence, it granted the Defence four months from the date of issuing of the Rule 98 bis Judgement to prepare its case. Bearing this in mind, the Trial Chamber stated its expectation that the Defence present thorough Pre-Defence case filings. With respect to some of the Pre-Defence case filings made on 13 May 2014, the Trial Chamber was concerned by the amount of errors contained therein. In an effort to ensure the efficient running of the Defence case, the Trial Chamber urge the parties to ensure that their filings are accurate and that all documents relied upon therein are provided within the set deadlines, along with translations where necessary. The Trial Chamber wishes the Defence to take further action in relation to the following pending motions: Defence motions for protective measures for witnesses. The Trial Chamber requested expedited disclosure of relevant confidential protective measures filings in relation to DGH-113 for the Defence. These filings were disclosed to the Defence on 12 June 2014. We would ask the Defence to make supplemental written submissions regarding the protective measures of DGH-113 by 20 June 2014. The Trial Chamber is also seized of the following pending motions: Defence motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts. Defence omnibus motion for the admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Defence omnibus motion for admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 quater. Prosecution motion directing the Defence to submit a revised Rule 65 ter witness list and witness summaries and for disclosure in accordance with Rule 67(A)(ii) and the Trial Chamber's orders. Prosecution motion to strike DGH-080 from the Defence Rule 65 ter witness list and the Defence motion to recall Witness Dusan Jaksic, the Trial Chamber will issue decisions on these matters in due course. In the meantime, we all have in our agenda that Defence case will commence on Thursday, 3 July 2014, at 9.00 a.m. in Courtroom III. The Trial Chamber shall commence with the opening statement of the Defence, pursuant to Rule 84 and with a Rule 84 bis statement by Mr. Hadzic. Immediately following the Defence opening statement, the Defence shall call its first witness. The Trial Chamber will sit five days per week during the months of July and August, save for the period of the Tribunal's summer recess. The sitting times shall be as follows: Session 1, 9.00, 10.30; session 2, 11.00, 12.15; session 3, 12.45, 1400, 2.00 p.m. Are there any other matters the parties wish to raise? Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have a proposal to have a -- four sitting days in July during the testimony of Mr. Hadzic. It -- it was the same criteria implemented during the whole Prosecution case. So we would like the Chamber, if it could modify this decision. Given the -- in particular, given the fact that the -- that Mr. Hadzic will be the only witness who will testify in three consecutive weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You do remember, Mr. Zivanovic, why we took this decision to sit five days -- days a week. At that moment, of course, we didn't know yet that Mr. Hadzic would be the first witness and, more or less, the only -- the only witness in -- in the month of July and probably part of August. Is -- has the Prosecution any -- anything to say on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Simply to observe, Mr. President, that although he is the accused, he is no different from any other witness, and the fact that it's the accused who is the witness is not, in our view, a justification for modifying the court schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll have to think about your proposal, Mr. Zivanovic, and we'll get back to the parties about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Any other matters? I thank the parties for their appearances and all other people involved for their support. We are moving into a new phase of this trial, and we very much appreciate the help of the supporting staff and the professional approach we experienced from both parties. This new phase in the trial will run, we hope, as efficiently as the previous one. The Pre-Defence Conference is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: at 9.20 a.m.
